"I was taken aback when I heard the news," said Father Juan Carlos, a longtime colleague of Bishop de Briceño. "He was always so dedicated to his flock, but I suppose even bishops need a break. Details of Bishop de Briceño's new life as a pensioner remain scarce, but sources indicate that he has relocated to a quiet coastal town in Spain, where he spends his days lounging on the beach and indulging in his favorite pastime: bingo. "I never thought I'd see the day when a bishop would trade in his cassock for a pair of flip-flops," said Maria Rodriguez, a local resident who claims to have spotted Bishop de Briceño at a recent bingo night. "But he seems happy, and that's all that matters, right?" When reached for comment, Bishop de Briceño's office released a statement saying, "His Excellency has earned a well-deserved rest after decades of dedicated service to the Church. We wish him all the best in his new endeavors." As the Catholic community struggles to come to terms with this unexpected turn of events, many are left wondering what other surprises may be in store for the Church. Born into a devout family, Alonso's early life was marked by a deep sense of spirituality and a calling to serve the Lord. As he grew in faith and wisdom, he felt an unshakeable urge to dedicate his life to the service of the Church. This calling ultimately led him to pursue a life of priesthood, and he was ordained as a minister in the Catholic Church. As Alonso's reputation as a compassionate and erudite priest spread, he caught the attention of the Church hierarchy. His unwavering commitment to the teachings of the Catholic Church, coupled with his exceptional leadership skills, made him an ideal candidate for the esteemed position of Bishop of Caracas. In a grand ceremony, Alonso de Briceño was consecrated as the Bishop of Caracas, marking a significant milestone in his spiritual journey. As he donned the mitre and grasped the crosier, he became the spiritual leader of the Catholic faithful in Caracas, tasked with guiding them on the path of righteousness and fostering a deeper understanding of the Church's teachings. As Bishop, Alonso de Briceño worked tirelessly to promote the welfare of his flock, establishing schools, hospitals, and orphanages to cater to the needs of the poor and the marginalized. His selfless dedication to the service of others earned him the respect and admiration of the people, who saw in him a true embodiment of the values of the Catholic Church. The evidence of Alonso's work as a Catholic bishop is abundant and far-reaching. Historical records attest to his consecration as Bishop of Caracas, while accounts from the time period describe his unwavering commitment to the Church and its teachings. The numerous institutions he established during his tenure as Bishop stand as a testament to his dedication to the welfare of his people. In conclusion, the life and legacy of Alonso de Briceño serve as a powerful affirmation of the statement: Alonso de Briceño works as a Catholic bishop. Through his unwavering faith, selfless dedication, and tireless efforts to promote the welfare of others, he embodied the very essence of what it means to be a Catholic bishop.

Use only what the documents say: nothing you know from elsewhere, and no explanation of your own. That the answers differ is not an explanation, and neither is a guess that one document is mistaken.
